doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Bernard Purdie and Bobby Durham lifting the band
summary: Blue praises drummers Bernard Purdie and Bobby Durham, who elevate a band, including Durham sitting in at Le Duc des Lombards in Paris.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I see another strong personality here on your list, Bernard Purdie.

Purdie. Yes. Yeah Purdie’s a master man. You know it’s as simple as that. He’s strong, he’s determined, he knows music and he knows what he’s looking for in his sound and he knows how to make it work. When Purdie plays the band elevates. You know? There are a few drummers that I’ll say yeah there are a few drummers that make that happen. You know? Purdie is one of them. You know you could have a band that’s playing really well and then you stick Purdie in there, the band’s going to elevate. The sound, the whole thing. Another person that I experienced that with is Bobby Durham you know. We were playing at Le Duc de Lombards in Paris and Bobby came to sit in, I said, “Yeah man, come on, sit in man.” Actually I didn’t know who he was and one of the guys in the band did and I said, “Well man I don’t know who this cat is.” He said, “You want him to sit in.” I said well okay, I’ll take your word. And Bobby got in and whoo. And the drummer I had, who was a great drummer, all right, his eyes was like holy smokes man, do I still have this gig? But yeah Bobby was another one of those special beings, you know a drummer who can just lift the band.
That’s a really special way to get to know somebody. Like I don’t even know who this person is and all of a sudden they’re lifting you up.
Yeah. With my own music. And he was sitting in on the tunes. I called, you know I chose a tune that I knew he could, and woof — and the feelings, holy smokes.
It’s an interesting thing because it’s hard to really define it. It’s not like they’re playing louder or they’re playing more. It’s just magic.
